mission_3.prediction: I tested the constrained map and first changed the repulsion strength for social_2 from 1.30 to 0.90, while keeping everything else unchanged. The robot still got stuck, but the failure changed from oscillation to an obstacle local minimum. So I then decided to reduce the influence distance from 1.50m to 1.00m, keeping the repulsion strength at 0.90 and the refinement step at 0.08m. After this change, the robot was finally able to find a complete path. The new path stayed close to the original one, with only small changes near the person. This shows that stronger repulsion and a larger influence distance don' t always improve the path since they can potentially cause our robot to get stuck.
mission_3.comparison:
For A*, social_2 had the largest minimum person clearance at 0.759 meters, compared to 0.706 meters for the baseline. It also reduced the time spent inside personal space from 1.8 seconds to 0 seconds. The execution time went down a little from 46.4 to 46.1 seconds, while the distance barely changed from 13.13 to 13.14.

For RRT, the baseline had the largest minimum clearance at 1.728 meters, compared to 1.722 meters for social_1 and 1.699 meters for social_2. All three spent 0 seconds inside personal space. The baseline was also the fastest at 43.3 seconds, compared to 44.6 seconds for social_2. This shows that stronger repulsion doesn't always make the route better, especially when the robot already stays far away from the person.
mission_3.recommendation: I would choose RRT with the baseline setting because it successfully reached the goal, had the largest minimum person clearance of 1.728 meters, and finished in 43.3 seconds. In comparison, A* with social_2 had a clearance of 0.759 meters and took 46.1 seconds . So RRT was both faster and stayed farther away from the person. With that being said, these trials only tested a person standing still. They can't tell us how the our robot would react if someone suddenly walked in front of it or changed direction. We would need to test it with moving people to see how well it performs in those situations.
